item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
For me, the issue is twofold:

First, there's the common use of the phrase "deems worthy" by itself. It is attempting to establish that its judgment is already superior to others for whatever reason. Oftentimes, it's more a sign that the object views itself too highly. It's only one step removed from the author thinking of themselves too highly, so tread carefully.

Second, there's a matter of the actual judgment criterion. In the end, all that's really said is the object will X if it likes you or not. No moral judgment. No soul-searching. Just arbitrary picking.

If you're going to use a judgment criterion, then you have to get into the head of the judge and focus on its feelings, independent of whatever you happen to think is right or wrong.

I think WJS means it along the lines of "X won't let you weild it/use it's powers/grant you knowledge unless it deems you worthy" instead of just "x that judges y".

While I don't think it is a SCP cliche of itself, it certainly is a classic cliche that quickly lends itself to becoming a bad SCP if not handled with care.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
You're both right and wrong.

To start this off, this article is old. Very old. Older than the mass edit. As I find myself constantly saying writing was a lot faster and looser than. I see this as the beginning of the stringent standards we have today. But yes, this is an old article and isn't as helpful as the modern resources. It's something to keep in mind.

In regards to what you actually said, I pretty much agree with you. A lot of these ideas are fine, if they're given enough originality to not be cliched. You're saying that from the perspective of a member who knows how to come up with tenable SCP ideas.

However, if a new writer were to come here and wanted to write something original that would stick, looking at this list would help them understand what's pretty common. It can help them figure out how where to take an idea to not match one of these stereotypes. Taken at face value and as general advice, it's fine. From a person who knows what they're doing, this list is just a curt reminder to give your concepts more thought. Now to address your specific comments.

+ show block
– hide block

Okay? What if it's a unique idea though? Not all movies are the exact same. Not all books are the exact same. It's perfectly fine for an author to take inspiration from someone else.

It's fine to take inspiration from tvs or movies. Hell, I do that all the time. The issue is taking things wholesale from other media. This was also written at a time where pop-culture based SCPs were not uncommon.

This didn't even need to be there.

I feel this was. It doesn't make much sense for an effect to occur from a sphere or cube. It's better to use an object related to the effect, to give the effect a bit more weight and provide a little implicit backstory.

The future is a very interesting topic because it holds so many possibilities. You can't go wrong with the future, and everyone's future can be different. There truly is no way to predict what the future will be like, and that's why authors choose to write SCP's based off the future.

That's entirely true. The issue lies when a writer tries to make the fact that the object is from the future the only interesting part of the SCP.

This idea can be done right if you read the other entries and focus on separating your concept from theirs. It's not too cliche.

Again this is true, but your suggestions show that you're thinking outside the box. Which a lot of new writers tend to not do.

item.content:encoded:
Looking on the SCPs as a whole, there are a few things that repeat.

Cats and dogs - house cats and corgis mostly,
THE MOON - with moon kings, wizards, factories, aliens and so on
Clowns - be they ordinary, naturally occurring, of Wonder-full make or H.Fuller-type
Jars - filled with non-jar stuff, like weather or dreams
and my favorite,
Common Saying - taken to literal extremes ("if you love it so much why don't you just eat it")

17Doctor, by "you" are you referring to the author of the page? If so, keep in mind there's no guarantee they'll see this comment. If you want feedback on an idea, you should ask in the Ideas and Brainstorming forum.

You see, I was thinking about writing about and SCP that is basically just an Island filled with talking Komodo Dragons or Platipi.

We have a couple of things like that. We have manta rays, at least one lion, and a bunch of other exotic animals capable of communication. "Weird talking animal(s)" on its own isn't usually enough to carry an article these days.

Nothing too dangerous, just something weird. How the Foundation would contain it, dunno.

If you're unsure about containment, try finding and reading some articles with similar anomalies to see how they handled containment.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
As divisive as this article is years later, I still think it serves a good purpose. Instead of scaring me off, back when I was a newbie, it helped me to focus my writing and make better articles.

When I joined in 2013, I had an interest in trying to write for the site. I began reading all of these kinds of articles. It helped me to focus in on ideas that were original… as well as understand that these cliches aren't off-limits, but rather just harder to do well. As long as you understand the core of what this article is trying to say, then you'll be fine (which is also why I think that reminder at the end is so crucial).

I would consider this one of the pieces that helped me in the long run. So some people may think it scares off the newbies, but I respectfully disagree.

item.title: Re: Not all...
item.content:encoded:
So even though some of these "cliches" are overused, I see no problem with that being they can still be their own SCP all on there own.

For the cliches on here (I don't feel like including quotations anymore at this point I'm about to be done) that I feel aren't overused, are not a bad thing either, for basically the same reason as previously said.

The definition of cliche, according to Google, is "a phrase or opinion that is overused and betrays a lack of original thought."

Cliches by definition are overused. That's the extent of it. This list even says at the top, "We got plenty of: […]" and then the point is furthered in the paragraphs at the end. It's not saying cliches are bad, wrong, [insert antagonistic synonym here]. It's saying that these things on the list are pretty overused, because, well… we've got a lot of them. And we probably will continue to have/get a lot of them.

Whether people think a cliche is bad is up to them. I personally am fine with having more butterfly SCPs. Also moths. We have a lot of them. Enough to merit their own tag, lepidopteran. Some may say it is cliche for people to keep writing butterfly SCPs because butterflies, and they are fully entitled to their opinion. This opinion does not change the fact that there are a substantial number of butterfly SCPs, compared to say, centipedes or pink tarantulas.

tl;dr, cliches are overused because that's part of what cliche means, doesn't necessarily mean ALWAYS BAD NEVER USE ANYTHING ON THIS LIST, methinks you're taking this too seriously.

Author, I feel as not all of the listed "cliches" on this page are completely overused and unoriginal. It depends on how you write your SCP, similar to what TheDuckman was saying. Although most of the "cliches" listed here I can agree with you are overused, I see no problem with that. For the overused "cliches" on here, are just the base structures for an SCP to base from. What really lies in a good SCP is its overall concept and/or story. So even though some of these "cliches" are overused, I see no problem with that being they can still be their own SCP all on there own. And I know you never directly mentioned overused "cliches" being a problem, but I felt the need to point that out anyway.
For the cliches on here (I don't feel like including quotations anymore at this point I'm about to be done) that I feel aren't overused, are not a bad thing either, for basically the same reason as previously said. So I feel I've made my point…

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
In line with changes elsewhere, I feel this could be updated by our current Guardians of Tone to be more helpful and specific regarding what cliches new writers especially should avoid. This is not as helpful a document as it could be. If we want to assist someone in avoiding a pitfall, couching it this deep in a series of outdated jokes isn't particularly productive in my opinion.

Also, it might be helpful to add "Things that are not usually sapient but now are". This is a very easy formula for people to follow, and while it can result in some interesting reads, it is very cliche. If "magic items" are cliche, I think this is a subset of magic items. "Object/Thing" + "Sapient" does not magically = good idea.
